envelope_assumptions.rotors: Finite solid swept circular slabs; not actual blade solids or calibrated flex envelopes
envelope_assumptions.tubes: Solid capsules enclose the ideal hollow tubes, including their extended endpoints
envelope_assumptions.spines: Each topology screened with maximum configured length and maximum candidate OD; no material or stock selection
envelope_assumptions.feet: Unselected spherical feet using the configured centre height and contact radius; no actual foot shape is established
envelope_assumptions.yoke: Four module-carried capsule hypotheses only; all crossmembers use the configured upright radius. No bearing, motor mount or joint interface is established
envelope_assumptions.scope_of_overlap: Outer-envelope overlap is not automatically intersection of actual hollow tubes or hardware
envelope_assumptions.scope_of_clear: Bounds apply only to declared rigid hypotheses, not omitted components or deformed hardware

continuous_bound_basis: For each in-cone alpha,beta, rounding both magnitudes toward zero reaches an included 1-degree grid point still inside the cone; each angular difference is at most one grid step.
Moving-envelope Hausdorff displacement is bounded by 2*sin(step/2)*(norm(d)+2*r_max), where r_max bounds every envelope point relative to the inner origin.
Axis-sampled distance lower bounds subtract half the sample spacing because distance to a closed set is 1-Lipschitz.
Ground support uses the finite cylinder support function and translates the complete rigid vehicle until its lowest modeled spherical foot touches the same plane.
The body-tilt bound covers every tilt from zero to the maximum configured tilt, not just endpoints, using nearest polar/azimuth vertical-covector samples and support-function radius bounds.
Floating-point calculations include a small explicit numerical debit but are not interval-arithmetic proofs; independent analytical fixtures and CAD reconciliation remain required.

limitations: This analysis does not rehabilitate the large-deflection unbraced landing-leg sensitivities from stage 1. Braced or otherwise revised load paths require their own geometry, mass, procurement and joint assessment.

Neither sampled overlaps nor loose continuous bounds justify an actuation-concept change. Retain the common gimbal and seek human agreement before any conflicting change.
No FCStd/STEP export, mounting acceptance, material qualification, complete vehicle mass/energy/cost result or review acceptance is produced.

A separate checker must test the actual configuration, program and results, including transform identities, noncoincident offsets, analytical support functions, deliberately colliding cases and convergence under finer sampling.
